speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I'm Dr. Agent. Can you tell me exactly when the swelling and pain in your right ring finger started, and did it follow any specific injury or insect bite?

speaker: Patient
text: 22-year-old male. The patient reports that the pain and swelling in his right ring finger began 2 days ago while playing football. He recalls his finger got caught in the jersey of another player, who then pulled away forcefully.

speaker: Doctor
text: Did you hear or feel a "pop" at the moment of injury, and are you currently able to fully extend the tip of your finger?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Progressive swelling and pain in the right ring finger. I also have Inability to flex the right ring finger at the distal interphalangeal joint when making a fist, Pain at the distal interphalangeal joint, Extended right ring finger in resting position.

speaker: Doctor
text: I see you have difficulty flexing the tip of your finger, which suggests a flexor tendon issue. Can you confirm if you can actively flex the distal interphalangeal joint at all, or is it completely stuck in extension? REQUEST TEST: X-Ray_Right_Hand

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: No bone fractures or dislocations visible. Soft tissue swelling noted around the distal interphalangeal joint of the right ring finger.

speaker: Doctor
text: The X-ray rules out a fracture, but your inability to actively flex the fingertip suggests a complete rupture of the flexor digitorum profundus tendon. Can you confirm that you cannot voluntarily bend the very last joint of your finger at all, even when trying to make a tight fist?

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: No significant medical history. Social history: Student and active in sports, particularly football. Non-smoker and drinks alcohol socially.

speaker: Doctor
text: Understood. To confirm the extent of the tendon injury, can you try to flex the middle joint (PIP) of your ring finger while keeping the other fingers straight? This will help determine if the flexor digitorum superficialis is also involved.

speaker: Patient
text: Denies fever, numbness, or tingling in the affected finger.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for the additional history. Since the X-ray ruled out fracture and you have no signs of infection or nerve involvement, I am confident in my assessment of the tendon injury. DIAGNOSIS READY: Jersey Finger (Flexor Digitorum Profundus Tendon Rupture)

DIAGNOSIS_READY_Answer: Rupture of the flexor digitorum profundus tendon at its point of insertion
